summary:
We developed IGNIS-PSI an interactive web based platform designed to make decades of NASA research on fire behavior in microgravity easier to access and understand using data from NASA’s Physical Science Informatics PSI database the platform brings complex scientific information into one place where researchers engineers and students can easily search filter compare and explore different combustion experiments

This becomes especially important as humanity prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars where spacecraft habitats and rovers may operate in environments with higher oxygen concentrations (≥30%) and lower pressures to make spacesuit transitions easier however these conditions can significantly increase the risk of fire ignition and flame spread compared to Earth

IGNIS-PSI aims to bridge the gap between NASA research and real world applications by making scientific data easier to understand and use helping researchers and engineers develop safer habitats and improve fire safety for future space missions
details:
IGNIS-PSI is an interactive web-based fire safety intelligence dashboard that makes decades of NASA microgravity combustion research from the Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database accessible and actionable.

  • Multi-Criteria Search and Filtering: Allows users to explore and filter NASA microgravity experiments such as BASS-II, Saffire, FLEX, and ACME based on fuel phase, mission hardware, and environmental parameters
  • Lunar and Martian Habitat Fire Risk Calculator: Provides interactive controls for cabin pressure and oxygen concentration to calculate ignition and flammability risk scores and identify relevant NASA experiments
  • AI-Powered Research Co-Pilot: Integrates Google Gemini API to answer complex engineering questions using NASA PSI research data with direct citations to relevant experiments
  • Engineering Report Generator: Generates and exports structured Markdown safety reports based on selected experiments and dashboard filters

Benefits and Intended Impact

As humanity prepares for sustained lunar exploration and future missions to Mars, spacecraft and habitats will face different atmospheric conditions, including higher oxygen concentrations (≥30%) and lower cabin pressures to facilitate spacesuit transitions. These conditions can significantly increase the risk of ignition and flame spread compared to Earth.

IGNIS-PSI transforms scattered scientific research into an accessible decision-support platform that helps mission planners, materials engineers, researchers, and students make informed decisions about spacecraft fire safety, material selection, smoke detection, and fire suppression systems.

Tools, Coding Languages and Software Used

  • Frontend and UI: React.js, TypeScript, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons
  • AI Integration: Google Gemini API
  • Deployment and Hosting: Railway
  • Development: AI-assisted development, component architecture, debugging, and data normalization

Live Application: https://nasa-web-production-e57f6536.up.railway.app/

Creativity and Key Factors Considered

IGNIS-PSI goes beyond traditional static research databases by introducing an interactive mission-control interface focused on simulation and decision support.

The development focused on three main factors:

  • Data Integrity: Organizing and verifying NASA research data to ensure reliable results and reduce inaccurate AI-generated information
  • Performance: Implementing client-side filtering for fast and responsive data exploration
  • Accessibility: Making complex aerospace combustion research easier to understand through interactive tools and visual risk indicators
